articles.title: I hiked 100 miles to find the best walking poles, here are my favourites
articles.summary: Trekking poles can improve balance on uneven terrain and reduce stress on joints. Our seasoned adventurer put 10 to the test to find the best. • ‘I’d never head out without one’: 10 hiking essentials. Oh, I would walk 500 miles – with the help of a trusty pole.
body: Hiking poles are typically used as a pair, and the idea is to swing each pole in time with the opposite foot as you move forwards: right foot and left pole, then left foot and right pole, in a rhythm. You can also use poles singly to keep a hand free or to take the weight off one side of your body.

Walking poles are available in fixed lengths or as adjustable models, and there are ones you can fold up and stick in a rucksack when not in use. There’s more variety out there than you may think – but we’ve narrowed it down to eight of the best walking poles for all kinds of hikers.

I’m a seasoned adventure travel writer and gear-tester, and I’ve been putting outdoor kit through its paces for more than a decade. I’ve hiked thousands of miles with walking poles – everywhere from the summit of Mount Kenya to my favourite local trails in the Cotswolds. I’ve also been working on two UK walking guides – a great excuse to grab a hiking pole and go exploring.
points: Trekking poles can improve balance on uneven terrain and reduce stress on joints.

articles.title: Why are garlic presses so out of fashion? | Kitchen aide
articles.summary: It’s the gadget people love to hate – but maybe it does have a place in the kitchen? Why are garlic presses suddenly a no-no? Recipes now stipulate grating instead, but who wants lumps of garlic in their dinner?
body: Christina Soteriou, recipe writer at Ottolenghi Inc and author of Big Veg Energy, however, takes a more balanced approach: “A garlic press is not necessarily a no-no, and there can definitely be a time and a place for it,” she says. “It’s definitely quicker [than chopping], but I’d use it only when said garlic is going into a sauce, stew or braise.” Which is to say, in a dish where those lumps that concern Sally will cook down and dissolve almost entirely.

As with most things in life, Sally should just do her, though Soteriou does suggest sticking to one rule: “A garlic press for anything that’s going to be slow-cooked, and a Microplane, pestle and mortar, or minced for anything where it will be raw or cooked very quickly.” Just “never, ever buy ready-crushed garlic”, Chandler says. “That’s another business altogether and it tastes awful.”

articles.title: 47 Easy Make-Ahead Thanksgiving Sides
articles.summary: Despite your most careful planning (did you make a detailed timeline?), cooking Thanksgiving dinner can still feel a little stressful once the big day rolls around. It holds true whether you’re having a small Thanksgiving dinner or hosting the whole extended family.
body: From classic stuffing to cozy and creamy casseroles, we’ve rounded up 47 make-ahead Thanksgiving sides that can be prepped, assembled, or even totally cooked anywhere from a day to a month in advance.

Stuffing is a great make-ahead side. Depending on your schedule and energy level, you’ve got a couple of options. For a head start, simply toast the bread up to several days in advance. Or if you prefer to tackle a little more, the whole dish can be prepped and assembled, then stashed in the fridge until you’re ready to slide it into the oven.

Roasted turkey gets the magazine covers and the big platters, but stuffing is the real star of the show. We're talking classic, herby, moist, and fragrant bread stuffing — just like your favorite boxed stuffing mix, but even better.

This hearty stuffing has all the flavors of French onion soup. It’s packed with deeply caramelized onions cooked low and slow until sweet and jammy, then topped with Gruyère cheese and broiled until melted and gooey.

articles.title: Autumn food stars: what to cook, plant and pick now
articles.summary: Cook up mushrooms, leeks and foraged chestnuts, pick fruit, sow broad beans for spring and harvest squash. Quince Hard as a baseball and initially unpromising, quince are at their best cooked until beautifully aromatic.
body: Leeks Try cooking these sweet, oniony joys in a moderate oven, wrapped in foil with just a dash of olive oil and a sliced garlic clove per leek, until soft and luscious – about 40 minutes, depending on thickness.

Apple Of the thousands of apple varieties, you’ll find only a few in the shops. For those with the best flavour and texture – including Egremont Russet, Worcester Pearmain, and Cox’s Orange Pippin – buy direct or from online suppliers, such as Riverford.

Squash As good as a standard butternut can be, Uchiki Kuri, crown prince and acorn table are a class apart and really worth looking for. Roast unpeeled and deseeded, with a little oil and earthy spices, until soft.

Porcini and chanterelles September and October are the best time to pick chanterelles (AKA girolles) and porcini (AKA ceps/penny buns), when warm weather followed by rain makes them most abundant. Take John Wright’s Mushrooms: River Cottage Handbook to identify them, or buy fresh fungi online.

articles.title: Jonathan Anderson mixes Austen romance with chic streetware in Dior’s Paris show
articles.summary: Designer’s latest work takes bold steps away from the fashion house’s brand, creating a show that felt like an event. “I want to land on a vibe.” This was how Dior designer Jonathan Anderson, one year into what is arguably the biggest job in fashion, summed up his assignment before his latest show.
body: “We are in search of a silhouette,” Anderson explained. The show began and ended with a distinctive shape: a short, kicky skirt in layers of chiffon, the layers catching the light like breaking surf, worn with a soft, short jacket or layers of sheer shirting. He is resistant to being pinned down to one look, though, so in between there were bronze metallic trousers, and luxurious double-breasted coats, and strapless bow-trimmed cocktail dresses tightly frilled as carnation petals.

“People have a preconceived idea of what Dior should be, and you don’t take the customer from zero to 100 overnight,” he said. His emotional tone is naturally bone-dry, but he is finding a take on “romantic” – a word that is central to Dior, and one that he kept returning to – where he can take that customer somewhere new. His idea of romance, he said, is Jane Austen. Romance, for Anderson, is never going to mean losing his head. If Dior is to get their happy ending, expect plenty of wry asides along the way.
points: Designer’s latest work takes bold steps away from the fashion house’s brand, creating a show that felt like an event.

articles.title: 23 Thanksgiving Turkey Recipes for Every Kind of Gathering
articles.summary: Whole birds, turkey breasts, braised legs, and more ways to rule the Thanksgiving table.
body: Picking a Thanksgiving turkey recipe is not very different from dating. Hear us out: There are plenty of great options, but you have to find the one that fits your life. How big is your gathering? How big is your oven? Should you even use the oven? Or is the grill calling your name? Maybe you're ready to venture away from your usual type. Or maybe you’re looking for something dependable, just this once.

If you want us to make the decision for you, start with our go-to Thanksgiving turkey: a whole bird dry-brined for juicy meat, slathered with butter, and finished with a tangy honey glaze for crispy, deeply browned skin. It’s the turkey we return to year after year.

But there's more than one way to put turkey on the Thanksgiving table. Spatchcocking means faster, more even cooking and plenty of crispy skin; turkey breast makes sense for a smaller gathering; braised legs put dark meat front and center; and a grilled or smoked turkey frees up precious oven space. Below, you’ll find 23 Thanksgiving turkey recipes for whatever kind of holiday you're hosting.
There’s the fast way, the better way—and one method that doesn’t require thawing at all.

articles.title: This Lakeside Town Was Just Named the Best 'Quietcation' in England
articles.summary: With hundreds of walking trails, peaceful lake views, and plenty of cozy tea rooms, Lake District's Windermere is the perfect place for a slowed down quietcation.
body: When I started traveling, I felt like I had to pack every day on holiday to the brim, but I often left feeling like I needed another to recover immediately afterwards. Now, unless I am traveling for work, I prefer a slower pace and days spent strolling around, people-watching, and really taking in the places I'm visiting—the traveler version of less is more, if you will.

The United Kingdom might not be the first place that comes to mind for island hopping or skiing, but it certainly is perfect for spending a few quiet days in nature. If your idea of a proper break involves switching off your phone, going for long walks, and generally doing as little as possible, a British quietcation might be exactly what you need.

The quietcation travel trend is all about escaping the noise and slowing things down, swapping packed itineraries and busy cities for nature, fresh air, and peaceful activities. No matter where you are, there are plenty of places across Britain where you can find the perfect setting for one.
points: With hundreds of walking trails, peaceful lake views, and plenty of cozy tea rooms, Lake District's Windermere is the perfect place for a slowed down quietcation.

articles.title: 24 Daytime Wedding Guest Dresses That Are Perfectly Appropriate
articles.summary: Wondering what to wear to an earlier wedding? A bridal stylist weighs in on the best daytime wedding guest dresses—from brands like Khaite, Staud, and more.
body: Most of us are accustomed to dressing for weddings that stretch well into the night. Move the celebration to daylight, however, and the usual evening formula—a floor-length gown, a little shimmer, a sleek black dress—reads as a total misstep. It’s a dilemma I know well from my years as a bridal stylist, and it usually prompts the same few questions: Is black still fair game? Is a mini appropriate? What, exactly, qualifies as daytime wedding guest attire?

The answer starts with the dress code. Take it at face value, then interpret it with a lighter hand—and a brighter palette—than you would after sunset. “Daytime formal,” for instance, still calls for long silhouettes, just without the heavy sequins of its evening counterpart. Where a structured black maxi can read decidedly somber at noon, a salmon-hued midi feels right at home at a midday cocktail fête. Ultimately, daylight demands you have fun with color, so don’t be afraid to embrace it.

articles.title: For Her Paris Fashion Week Debut, Fidan Novruzova Makes a Case for Vanity
articles.summary: Spring 2027 sees the Azerbaijani-Moldovan designer soften her signatures, play with color and proportion, and reframe vanity as a celebration of self.
body: Six years after launching her namesake label, Fidan Novruzova is thinking about vanity. Not, however, as one of the less attractive human impulses, but as something more gentle and liberating—the pleasure of looking, dressing, and indulging oneself. “There’s a way of thinking about your desires and your ego,” the Azerbaijani-Moldovan designer says from Paris the day before she makes her official Paris Fashion Week calendar debut, “in a way that it celebrates you.”

Her spring 2027 collection is fittingly titled La Vanité. But for a designer whose work has steadily accrued its own unmistakable codes—exaggerated square-toed boots, interesting collars, and rigorously sculpted outerwear—this season represents a moment of newfound confidence.

“I’m trusting that whatever I’m going to do is going to be me,” says Novruzova. Earlier in her career, she remembers questioning whether each experiment looked sufficiently “on brand.” Now, “I feel like I’ve been doing things that I would’ve not done five seasons ago, and I’m totally at peace doing and trying and loving something … or hating something that I’m doing.”
